title: Chunkwise trace-slices and PII shepherding for backpressure-aware streaming observability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a per-chunk observability subsystem that captures compact telemetry slices and short-lived tracing spans for streamed responses while ensuring PII never leaves the redaction boundary. The feature targets streaming API flows (HTTP chunked, SSE, websockets) and must gracefully degrade for legacy clients that only support polling. Key goals: (1) attach a lightweight trace ID per logical chunk range, (2) emit summarized per-chunk metrics (token_count, emission_latency_ms, backpressure_ms, tool_call_count, error_flag), (3) integrate a privacy-first redaction pipeline that scrubs sensitive tokens before they are persisted to logs/metrics, and (4) provide a compatibility shim that maps chunk slices to older non-streaming trace models for downstream dashboards and alerting.
acceptance_criteria: Compact per-chunk telemetry emitted for >= 95% of streamed responses under normal load without increasing 95th latency by >5%
Tracing spans open/close per chunk-range and correlate to parent request in tracing backend (span links present in Jaeger/Datadog)
Redaction layer removes or tokenizes PII patterns (SSN-like, email, API keys) before any telemetry export; unit tests demonstrate false positive rate < 1% on synthetic corpus
Backward compatibility: non-streaming dashboards can reconstruct an equivalent request timeline from chunk slices with <200ms reconstruction error on timestamps
Feature gated behind flags and rolloutable by region with metrics and rollback hooks defined
design_notes: We will model each streamed response as an ordered sequence of "ChunkSlices". Each ChunkSlice carries a small metadata envelope (slice_index, start_token_idx, end_token_idx, slice_token_hash) but the payload is never stored in plain form. A two-stage redaction approach will be used: (A) fast inline heuristics for high-confidence PII (emails, long hex/blobs, JWT/API-key patterns) applied pre-export, and (B) async deeper scrubbers that run on sampled slices with richer ML-based detectors for contextual PII. To avoid tail latency regressions, the inline heuristics must be O(n) with a very small constant and operate under a fixed CPU budget per request. For tracing, a span is opened at slice emission start and closed after confirmation of network flush or after backpressure timeout. Spans are annotated with compact numeric codes for common tool calls to avoid free-text leakage. Compatibility shim: a reconstruct endpoint that ingests chunk metadata streams and produces a synthetic non-streaming trace event for dashboards. See prototype diagram in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/STREAM-V2-ARCH
implementation_plan: spec: finalize ChunkSlice envelope and telemetry schema (schema id v2-chunk-2026)
runtime: add lightweight inline redactor using regex+trie (C++ runtime change, feature-flagged)
tracing: open/close per-slice spans and add span-linking to parent request (SDK + runtime)
exporter: telemetry aggregator service to receive compact slice metrics and perform sampling for deep-scrub queue
compatibility: implement reconstruct endpoint and a client shim that maps legacy polling traces
QA: synthetic load test with haproxy replay, privacy fuzz tests, and e2e tracing validation
testing_plan: Unit tests for inline redaction with curated PII examples
Fuzz corpus run to identify false positives/negatives for inline heuristics
Load test: simulate 10k concurrent streaming sessions and assert 95th percentile token latency regression < 5%
Integration test: end-to-end span correlation into our tracing backend (Datadog) using a test agent
Backward-compatibility test: reconstruct endpoint produces accurate non-stream timeline for dashboard replay
rollout_plan: Feature will be gated behind runtime feature-flag `chunk_obsv_v2`. Rollout phases: 1) internal-only (team alpha) for 48h, 2) customer beta for selected accounts (region us-east-1) for 2 weeks with telemetry thresholds, 3) gradual 25% -> 50% -> 100% across regions. Automated canary rollback: if per-region alert rate for telemetry errors > 0.5% or token-latency regression > 8% on 95th, auto-disable flag and notify SRE.
